title: Muscle strength in COPD patients and its association with sarcopenia
summary:
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a progressive respiratory condition that affects not only the lungs but the entire body. A common comorbidity is sarcopenia – a disease-related loss of muscle mass and strength that can lead to reduced physical performance.

The aim of this study is to examine the muscle strength of COPD patients and to analyze its association with quality of life.

interventions.name:
Collection and implementation of:
1. Medical history and assessment of patient history
2. Handgrip strength measurement
3. BORG scale (degree of dyspnea)
4. mMRC (modified dyspnea scale)
5. SRI (Severe Respiratory Insufficiency Questionnaire)
6. SARC-F (screening tool for sarcopenia)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a known diagnosis of COPD (all GOLD stages) and type 2 respiratory failure

Adherence to guideline-based pharmacological therapy

Consent to the data protection policy and provision of written informed consent

Cognitive and linguistic ability to complete the questionnaires
Exclusion criteria:
Age < 18 years

Patients lacking capacity to give informed consent

Rheumatoid arthritis or other chronic inflammatory joint diseases with relevant involvement of the wrists or finger joints

Carpal tunnel syndrome or comparable peripheral nerve compression syndromes of the upper extremity

Chronic polyneuropathies with sensorimotor involvement of the hands

Corticosteroid-induced or primary myopathies

Neurological disorders with impaired hand motor function (e.g., Parkinson's disease, status post cerebrovascular insult, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis)

Cervical radiculopathies or plexopathies with documented muscle weakness in the dominant hand

Musculoskeletal disorders or acute pain syndromes of the hand or forearm (e.g., tenosynovitis, advanced osteoarthritis)

Recent injuries, surgeries, or other conditions that may interfere with standardized grip strength testing
